evals.prompt: Help me plan a paid advertising strategy. We're a B2B SaaS tool for HR teams, selling at $99/month per seat. We have $15k/month to spend on ads and want to generate demo requests. Where should we advertise?
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should apply the platform selection guide based on B2B, HR audience, $99/month price point. Should recommend LinkedIn (B2B targeting by job title/industry), Google Ads (search intent for HR software keywords), and potentially Meta (retargeting). Should recommend campaign structure with naming conventions. Should define audience targeting strategy for each platform. Should set budget allocation across platforms. Should define success metrics and attribution approach. Should recommend starting structure and scaling plan.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing.md
Applies platform selection guide
Recommends platforms appropriate for B2B HR audience
Recommends campaign structure with naming conventions
Defines audience targeting per platform
Sets budget allocation across platforms
Defines success metrics
Recommends starting structure and scaling plan

evals.prompt: Our Google Ads CPC is $12 and our cost per lead is $180. Is that good? We're getting about 80 leads/month from a $15k budget.
evals.expected_output: Should evaluate the metrics in context. Should assess: $12 CPC for B2B (reasonable depending on industry), $180 CPL (depends on LTV — need to compare against customer lifetime value), 80 leads/month from $15k (math checks out). Should apply the campaign optimization framework: check quality score, search term relevance, landing page conversion rate, negative keywords. Should recommend specific optimization levers to reduce CPC and CPL. Should frame performance against industry benchmarks if applicable. Should ask about downstream conversion rates (lead → demo → customer).
assertions: Evaluates metrics in context
Compares CPL against LTV considerations
Applies campaign optimization framework
Recommends specific optimization levers
Asks about downstream conversion rates
Provides industry context for benchmarking

evals.prompt: we want to run retargeting ads for people who visited our site but didn't convert. how should we set this up?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger on casual phrasing. Should apply the retargeting strategies section, specifically the funnel-based approach. Should recommend audience segments: all visitors (broad), pricing page visitors (high intent), blog readers (lower intent), and cart/signup abandoners (highest intent). Should recommend different messaging and offers for each segment. Should address frequency capping to avoid ad fatigue. Should recommend retargeting platforms (Meta, Google Display, LinkedIn). Should include duration windows for each audience.
assertions: Triggers on casual phrasing
Applies funnel-based retargeting approach
Recommends audience segments by intent level
Recommends different messaging per segment
Addresses frequency capping
Recommends retargeting platforms
Includes audience duration windows

evals.prompt: Should we advertise on TikTok? We sell accounting software to small businesses. Our current ads are on Google and Meta.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the platform selection guide for TikTok specifically. Should suggest a small test budget approach if they want to try.

Evaluates fit for accounting + small business audience
Provides honest assessment of likely weaker fit

evals.prompt: Can you write some ad copy for our Facebook ads? We need headlines and descriptions for 5 different angles.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is an ad creative generation task, not campaign strategy. Should defer to or cross-reference suede-ad-creative, which handles platform-specific ad copy generation with character limits, angle-based variation, and batch generation. May provide brief ad copy framework guidance but should make clear that suede-ad-creative is the right skill for generating ad copy at scale.
assertions: Recognizes this as ad creative generation
References or defers to suede-ad-creative
Does not attempt bulk ad copy generation using campaign strategy patterns

evals.prompt: We sell a $49/month meal-planning app. I want to run a Meta ad sequence on our Sales campaign: hook ad, then a problem ad, then a testimonial, then the offer. How do I set that up?
evals.expected_output: Should load references/meta-ad-sequencing.md (linked from the SKILL.md section on Meta in the Andromeda era) and explain that explicit ad sequencing is not available on Sales (or Leads) objectives: it requires Awareness (Maximize reach) or Engagement (ThruPlay), Target frequency rather than a cap, a lifetime budget at the ad set level of at least 7 days with Advantage campaign budget off, and at least two ads. Should offer two routes: a sequencing campaign on an eligible objective for the top of the path, or approximating the path on the Sales campaign with engagement retargeting (hook-ad video viewers get the proof ad, then the offer). Should size the sequence to the flight (campaign length and frequency window cap how many ads fit) and suggest trimming four ads to two or three. Should note target frequency usually costs more per impression, so judge on downstream conversions, ideally against a holdout, and tell the user to confirm the current setup in Meta's help docs.
assertions: States that sequencing is not available on the Sales objective
Lists the setup requirements: Awareness or Engagement objective, target frequency, lifetime budget of 7+ days, 2+ ads
Offers engagement retargeting as the way to approximate the path on a conversion campaign
Explains that flight length and frequency cap how many ads fit, and suggests 2-3 ads
Flags the higher cost per impression and says to judge on downstream conversions
Does not cite an unverified conversion multiplier for sequencing

evals.prompt: We pay $200/month for an ad spy tool and mostly use it to see what our 6 competitors are running. Can we build our own that updates every week?
evals.expected_output: Should load references/competitor-ad-tracker.md and lay out the pipeline: widen the competitor list, pull active ads on a schedule from the Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency Center and LinkedIn Ad Library, store the creative, tag each ad with a vision-capable model (hook, angle, offer, format, length, first and last seen), write to a database, diff weekly, and ask gap questions. Should note that Meta's official Ad Library API only returns all ads for EU delivery and political or issue ads elsewhere, and the other libraries have no official API, so most builds use a scraping API or actor, subject to each source's terms. Should treat long-running ads as a proxy for what is working, not proof. Should frame build vs. buy neutrally (subscription vs. maintenance) without declaring a winner, and say to adapt angles, never copy ads.
assertions: Describes a scheduled pull, store, tag, database, weekly-diff pipeline
States the Meta Ad Library API limitation (all ads only for EU delivery, otherwise political or issue ads)
Mentions checking each source's terms when scraping
Treats ad longevity as a proxy, not proof that an ad wins
Frames build vs. buy as a trade-off without recommending one as best
Says to adapt competitors' angles, not copy their ads

evals.prompt: B2B SaaS, Google Search spend around $6k/month, about 12 conversions a month across all campaigns, manual CPC on phrase and exact. Our Google rep says we should turn on AI Max. Should we?
evals.expected_output: Should load references/google-search-playbook.md and apply the broad-match gate to AI Max: 30+ conversions per month in the campaign, smart bidding live, and a tight negative list. At about 12 conversions a month across the account on manual CPC, the account fails the gate, so the answer is not yet. Should explain what AI Max does (matches beyond the keyword list, rewrites ad text, can send clicks to other pages via final URL expansion) and the B2B risk of landing buyers on careers or blog pages. Should give the conditions for a later test: URL exclusions, reviewing search terms and chosen landing pages weekly, and comparing against a campaign without it.
assertions: Applies the same gate as broad match (30+ conversions/month, smart bidding, negatives)
Concludes the account is not ready for AI Max yet
Explains final URL expansion and the risk of sending B2B clicks to the wrong pages
Lists URL exclusions, weekly search-term and landing-page review, and a comparison campaign as test conditions
